genEdNote: Some General Education credits may be met by major courses. A completed VCCS associate degree satisfies JMU General Education.

groups.label: Introductory programming
groups.note: B- or better to continue to CS 159 and CS 227.

groups.label: Calculus
groups.note: Take calculus early; MATH 231 or equivalent is a prerequisite for CS 240.

groups.label: Statistics
groups.note: Recommended in the second year; needed for CS 412/452.

groups.label: Systems elective
groups.note: Take the systems elective before your final semester when you can. CS 432 is offered in fall only.

groups.label: CS electives
groups.note: 9 credits of CS at the 300 level or above, with at least two courses above CS 332. Courses used for another requirement don't count twice.

groups.label: General Education
groups.note: The Human Community (41 credits): 14 domains in five areas. Satisfied by a completed associate degree. Madison Foundations (C1) must be finished by the end of the first year at JMU.

groups.label: University electives
groups.note: 8 three-credit university electives (24 credits) taken at JMU. Transfer credit doesn't count. Any JMU course no other requirement uses counts, including extra CS courses beyond the 9 CS elective credits; General Education placeholders don't.

groups.label: Credit residency
groups.note: To earn a bachelor's degree, at least 50% of required hours must be earned through enrollment at JMU and/or accepted transfer credit from four-year institutions, and at least 25% must be earned at JMU. Community college, exam (AP/IB), and military credit count toward the rest.

gradeRules: CS 149 and CS 227 need a B- or better to continue in the major.
A C- or better is required in CS 240, CS 261, CS 327, CS 361, calculus, and statistics.
Cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 in major courses.
CS 149, CS 159, CS 240, and CS 261 may each be attempted at most twice.
Credit/no-credit may not be used for major courses or CS electives.

advisingTips.Year 1: Use the CS advising Canvas site and the CS wiki, attend advising events, meet your advisor, use TA hours, and explore clubs and the CISE career fair. Apply to the major the semester you take CS 159 and CS 227 (or your first semester if you transfer in beyond them).
advisingTips.Year 2: Attend advising events, plan junior and senior electives, set up Handshake, build an online presence, attend the September and February career fairs, and apply for summer internships.
advisingTips.Year 3: Attend advising events and career fairs, look for leadership roles, volunteer, pursue internships or department research, and plan for the GRE if considering graduate school.
advisingTips.Year 4: Apply to graduate by mid-October for May graduation, attend the September career fair, build projects, apply for full-time jobs, and use on-campus recruiting.

avoidTogether.reason: CS 240 and CS 261 are both demanding gateway courses with a C- minimum and a two-attempt limit; taking them in separate terms is recommended.
